identity.author: John Davenant
identity.work: Two Dissertations (De praedestinatione through Cap. X Arg. X)
identity.edition: Dissertationes duae (Cambridge: Roger Daniel, 1650). Partial through Cap. X Arg. X (Ambrose/Basil). Further Cap. X remains.

scope.locus: De praedestinatione Cap. X Arg. X cont. (gratis data / Aug / Prov / Ambrose / Basil).
scope.next_locus: Cap. X Arg. X close / Corvinus reply (Contra Tilen. p.148) then Ultimum argumentum (councils vs Pelagians).

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. X cont.: if 1 Cor. iv. 7 holds of gratia gratis data, much more of justifying grace and of the first grace of election to life
english: If that holds of gratia gratis data, as the School calls it, it holds much more of the grace that makes acceptable—and most of all of that first grace of election to life, the fountain and spring of every benefit that serves salvation.
sections.latin: Si hoc in gratia gratis data (ut Schola loquitur) verum sit, tum multo magis in gratia gratum faciente, et maxime omnium in prima illa gratia electionis ad vitam, quae fons est et quasi scaturigo beneficiorum omnium ad salutem conferentium.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. X: Augustine De praedest. sanct. 5 — common gifts do not discern; the grace that discerns good from evil is not common; God discerns you from another
english: Hear Augustine keeping Paul’s steps and teaching (De praedestinatione sanctorum 5): Are men set apart from men by gifts common to all? A little later: The grace that sets the good apart from the evil is not common to both. Still plainer: God sets you apart from another, to whom he has not given what he gave you.
sections.latin: Sed audiamus Augustinum Pauli vestigiis et doctrinae inhaerentem: De praedest. sanct. cap. 5. Numquid, inquit, per haec dona, quae omnibus communia sunt hominibus, discernuntur homines ab hominibus? Paulo post, Gratia quae bonos discernit a malis, non communis est et bonis et malis. Adhuc planius; Deus te discernit ab alio, cui non donavit, quod donavit tibi.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. X: elect/non-elect divide arises from God’s diverse decrees of preparing and giving—not from human operations about commonly offered grace; Arminius intolerable
english: From all this it is plain: the divide of elect and non-elect, believers and unbelievers, those who persevere and those who do not, does not arise from prior, distinct human-will operations about commonly offered grace, but from God’s prior, diverse decrees and workings—decreeing, preparing, and giving to one what he neither decreed nor prepared nor gave to the other. So Arminius’s view is intolerable: it credits God with a common preparation and offer of grace, but credits each person’s free will, stirred by that common grace, with the very discrimination of believers and unbelievers, elect and non-elect.
sections.latin: Ex quibus omnibus manifestum est, Discrimen electorum et non-electorum, credentium et non-credentium, perseverantium et non-perseverantium oriri non ex antecedaneis et discretis humanarum voluntatum circa gratiam communiter oblatam operationibus, sed ex antecedaneis et diversis Dei decretis et operationibus, in decernendo, praeparando et donando uni quod non decrevit, neque praeparavit neque donavit alteri. Intoleranda est igitur Arminii sententia, quae ad Deum refert communem quandam gratiae praeparationem et oblationem, ad singulorum autem hominum liberum arbitrium hac communi gratia excitatum refert ipsam discriminationem credentium et non-credentium, electorum et non-electorum.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. X Major/Minor: non-elect = those to whom God never destined efficacious means; many such exist; therefore many are passed by before foresight of final unbelief
english: As for everlasting life: the one passed by, non-elect, or reprobate before foresight of his unbelief is the one to whom God from eternity neither destined nor prepared, and in time did not give, efficacious means to beget faith and perseverance and obtain everlasting life infallibly. But to many—as the event itself shows—God neither destined nor prepared nor gave that efficacious grace. Therefore many are passed by or non-elect before foresight of their unbelief and final stubbornness in it. The Minor is beyond dispute; so let us open and confirm the Major.
sections.latin: Quod attinet ad vitam aeternam, ille antecedenter ad praevisam suam infidelitatem praeteritus, non-electus, sive reprobatus consideratur, cui Deus ab aeterno non destinavit, praeparavit, ac cui in tempore non donavit efficacia media ad fidem et perseverantiam ingenerandam, vitamque aeternam infallibiliter obtinendam: At multis (sicut eventus ipse declarat) Deus nec destinavit, nec praeparavit, nec donavit hanc gratiam efficacem. Ergo, multi sunt praeteriti sive non-electi antecedenter ad praevisam suam infidelitatem et contumaciam finalem in eadem. De Minore nulla potest esse quaestio: Majorem igitur explicemus et confirmemus.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. X Major: God knows infinite modes to turn any heart; to deny this denies omnipotence — Prov. xxi. 1; Augustine De corr. et grat. 14
english: First I take this: God knows infinite ways to bend any man’s heart to repent, believe, and persevere freely. Who denies it denies God’s omnipotence and his absolute lordship over human wills—against Solomon (Prov. xxi. 1): The king’s heart is in the Lord’s hand; he turns it wherever he wills. Augustine subscribes (De correptione et gratia 14): Of men’s very wills he does what he wills, when he wills, holding most omnipotent power to incline human hearts wherever he wills.
sections.latin: Illud imprimis sumo; Deum nosse infinitos modos quibus cor cujuscunque hominis flectere possit ad libere poenitendum, credendum, et perseverandum. Qui hoc negat, negat Dei omnipotentiam, negat Dei supra voluntates humanas absolutum dominium, contra illud Solomonis, Cor regis in manu Domini; quocunque voluerit inclinavit illud, Prov. xxi. 1. Cui subscribit Augustinus, De corrept. et gratia, cap. 14. De ipsis hominum voluntatibus facit quod vult, et quando vult, habens humanorum cordium quo vult inclinandorum omnipotentissimam potestatem.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. X: he who could bend Judas as Peter, yet destined the means to Peter not Judas, elected one and reprobated the other — Ambrose: God calls whom he deigns
english: Add this: he who knew and could apply to Judas as to Peter the means to bend him to faith and obedience and keep him in them to the end, yet from eternity destined and gave those means to Peter and neither destined nor gave them to Judas, elected one to salvation and passed the other by—that is, reprobated him. That is what Ambrose meant in the famous saying: God calls whom he deigns, and makes religious whom he wills—words Augustine weighs carefully (De gratia Christi contra Pelagium et Caelestium 1.46).
sections.latin: Hisce addo, Illum qui novit et potuit adhibere tam Judae quam Petro ea media, quibus ad fidem et obedientiam flecteretur, et in fide et obedientia ad extremum usque conservaretur, atque haec media Petro ab aeterno destinavit et donavit, Judae nec destinavit nec donavit, unum eorum elegisse ad salutem, alterum praeteriisse, id est, reprobasse. Hoc illud est quod Ambrosius celebri illo dicto innuabat, Deus quos dignatur vocat, et quem vult religiosum facit. Quae verba accurate expenduntur ab Augustino, De grat. Christi contra Pelag. et Caelest. lib. 1. cap. 46.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. X: Basil and Isa. xlvi. — when God wills he saves and none resists; those not effectually called lack that unfrustrable will to convert and save
english: Basil agrees, in an oration Peter the Deacon reports (De incarnatione et gratia 8): Give, Lord, strength and safeguard. Make good the evil you take; keep the good in goodness—for you can do all things, and none contradicts you. When you will, you save, and none resists you. Both learned it from the Prophet on the divine will (Isa. xlvi. 10–11): The Lord of hosts has sworn: It shall be as I thought; as I planned in mind, so it shall happen. The Lord of hosts has decreed—and who can weaken it? From all this I infer: for those not called with an efficacious call, not made religious, not kept in faith and holy obedience—in a word, not actually saved—God lacked that unfrustrable will to convert them, make them religious and faithful, keep them in faith, and at last save them in fact.
sections.latin: Hisce consonat illud Basilii, in oratione quadam quae refertur a Petro Diacono, lib. De incarn. et grat. cap. 8. Dona, Domine, virtutem ac tutamentum. Malos, quos sumis, bonos facito; bonos in bonitate conservato: omnia enim potes, et non est qui contradicat tibi. Cum enim volueris, salvas, et non est qui resistat tibi. Uterque a Propheta hoc didicit, qui de voluntate divina ita nos instituit, Isa. xlvi. 10 et 11. Juravit Dominus exercituum, Si non ut putavi ita erit, et quomodo mente tractavi ita eveniet. Dominus exercituum decrevit, et quis poterit infirmare? Ex hisce omnibus infero, quod eos qui non vocantur vocatione efficaci, et qui religiosi non efficiuntur, qui non in fide et sancta obedientia conservantur; uno verbo, qui reapse non salvantur, defuisse Deo illam voluntatem et infrustrabilem eos convertendi, religiosos et fideles efficiendi, in fide conservandi, atque tandem de facto salvandi.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. X close toward Corvinus: opposite for the elect — eternal saving will proves election/preterition; foresight cannot ground either special will or its denial
english: Conversely, of those made religious, faithful, persevering, and led to everlasting life, we may gather that from eternity God had that will which would efficaciously work all this in them. That will to save—and non-will, if one may so speak—plainly proves election of some and preterition of others. Finally: as it would be inept to claim that the special will to work faith, perseverance, and salvation in Peter flowed from foresight of Peter’s faith and perseverance, so it is no less false and inept to assert that the denied will to effect faith, repentance, and perseverance in Judas or any reprobate arose from foresight of his unbelief, impenitence, and final contempt of divine grace.
sections.latin: sicut e contra, quoad eos qui religiosi, fideles, perseverantes efficiuntur, et ad vitam aeternam perducuntur, colligere possumus ab aeterno adfuisse Deo illam voluntatem, quae haec omnia in illis efficaciter operaretur. Haec autem voluntas salvandi, et noluntas (si ita loqui liceat) electionem aliquorum et praeteritionem aliorum manifeste evincit. Denique, sicut ineptum esset obtendere hanc specialem voluntatem de fide, perseverantia et salute Petri operanda ex praevisa ejusdem Petri fide et perseverantia profluxisse, ita non minus falsum et ineptum est asserere, hanc negatam voluntatem efficiendi fidem, poenitentiam et perseverantiam in Juda, aut quolibet reprobato, ex praevisa ejusdem infidelitate, impoenitentia et finali gratiae Divinae contemptu originem habuisse.
